issues.t: Engine stalls when fuel pump fuse blows (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly stalls while driving or won't start, as if it ran out of fuel. Some owners find the fuel pump fuse blown, sometimes again after replacing it.
issues.why: The wiring for the fuel tank temperature sensor can be routed wrong, rub through and short out, which blows the fuel pump fuse. The recall covers 2013-2021 NV200 vans, NV200 Taxis and the 2015-2018 Chevrolet City Express, which is the same van.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls (City Express owners too). Dealers reroute the harness or replace the fuel pump assembly for free. Don't keep replacing the fuse or install a bigger one.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may switch off (recall)
issues.sym: The Passenger Air Bag Off light is lit even with an adult in the seat, so the front passenger airbag would not deploy.
issues.why: The occupant classification system in the passenger seat can misread an adult as a child or an empty seat. Nissan recalled 2013-2016 NV200s and NV200 Taxis and 2015-2016 Chevrolet City Express vans to replace the sensor's control unit.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free repair. Until then, don't let a passenger ride up front if the Off light stays on with an adult in the seat.

issues.t: Airbag light from passenger seat sensor fault
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on or flashes, sometimes with the Passenger Air Bag Off light acting oddly.
issues.why: The occupant detection sensor in the passenger seat sets a fault code. Nissan has a bulletin for this code and offered a retrofit of the sensor system on 2013-2016 vans.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read by a dealer or a shop with Nissan software. Airbags may not work properly while the light is on.

issues.t: A/C water leaks into the center console
issues.sym: Water drips or puddles around the center console or front floor when the air conditioning runs.
issues.why: Condensation from the A/C can leak into the console area where the airbag control unit sits. Nissan ran service campaigns to add console insulation and to deal with liquid getting into the airbag control unit.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan or Chevrolet dealer to check your VIN for the console insulator and airbag control unit campaigns. Dry the area and don't ignore an airbag light after a leak.

issues.t: Wiring harness short can stop the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off and the van loses electrical power, often after a blown main fuse.
issues.why: On 2013 vans built from February to August 2013, a wiring harness could rub through against the fusible link bracket and short out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Dealers reposition the harness and add protective covering under the recall.

issues.t: Steering column may come apart (recall)
issues.sym: Looseness or clunking in the steering wheel, and in the worst case loss of steering.
issues.why: On some 2013 vans the steering column was not put back together correctly after a factory inspection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the free inspection done. Don't drive the van if the steering feels loose.

issues.t: Backup camera image can be switched off (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture doesn't appear when you shift into Reverse, or it flickers.
issues.why: A display setting could turn off the rearview image, and it stayed off in Reverse.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; dealers update the camera software for free. Use your mirrors and check behind the van until it is fixed.

issues.t: Tires wearing out early or cupping
issues.sym: Tires wear out in 15,000 to 25,000 miles, with uneven or cupped tread and growing road noise, even after alignments.
issues.why: This is the most reported NV200 complaint. Owners blame alignment settings and heavy work use; the exact cause has not been confirmed by Nissan.
issues.next: Rotate tires every 5,000 miles, keep them at the pressure on the door sticker for your load, and get a full alignment check. Ask for printouts showing before and after settings.

issues.t: CVT noise or poor operation (torque converter campaign)
issues.sym: Clattering or rattling from the transmission, shudder, or the van not driving smoothly.
issues.why: Nissan ran a voluntary campaign to replace the torque converter in the CVT (continuously variable transmission) on some vans.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN for open transmission campaigns. Have the CVT fluid checked; this transmission has no dipstick, so it needs a shop.

issues.t: CVT judder with transmission trouble codes
issues.sym: Shudder or jerky acceleration, sometimes with the check engine light and stored transmission codes.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin for CVT codes related to judder and pressure control, usually fixed with a software update or valve body work.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about the transmission bulletin and any software updates before agreeing to a full transmission replacement.

issues.t: Check engine light for EVAP leak
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with codes such as P0456 or P0455, but the van drives normally. Some owners also have trouble filling the tank.
issues.why: Nissan traced many small fuel-vapor leaks to a bad O-ring on the EVAP vent control valve, and other cases to the fuel cap or canister.
issues.next: Tighten or replace the fuel cap first. If the light returns, ask the shop to check the vent control valve O-ring named in Nissan's bulletin.

issues.t: Check engine light for air flow sensor (P0101)
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0101, sometimes with hesitation or weak acceleration.
issues.why: Nissan has a bulletin specific to the NV200 and NV200 Taxi for this mass air flow sensor code.
issues.next: Ask the shop to follow the Nissan bulletin before replacing parts. Check that the air filter and intake duct are sealed and clean.

issues.t: Clicking from axles when pulling away
issues.sym: A click or tick from a front wheel area when you start moving or accelerate from a stop.
issues.why: Nissan's bulletin points to the joint between the axle and the wheel hub, which is fixed by cleaning and applying a special grease.
issues.next: Mention Nissan's axle clicking bulletin to the shop. If the noise is a clicking only in turns, have the CV joints checked too.

issues.t: Clunk or pop from front strut when steering
issues.sym: A clunk, pop or knock from the top of a front strut when turning the steering wheel, especially at low speed.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin for noise from the upper strut mount area on these vans.
issues.next: Have the strut mounts and bearings inspected. Replacing the mount parts named in the bulletin usually quiets it.

issues.t: No start after sitting in freezing weather
issues.sym: After the van sits overnight below freezing, it won't start, and a communication code (U1000) is stored.
issues.why: Nissan identified a cold-soak no-start condition linked to network communication between control units.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for the bulletin fix. Make sure the 12-volt battery tests healthy, since a weak battery makes cold starts worse.

issues.t: Worn key won't turn the ignition
issues.sym: The key won't turn, or you have to wiggle it to start the van.
issues.why: Heavy daily use wears the key blade. Nissan's bulletin says to replace the worn key rather than the ignition switch.
issues.next: Try your spare key. If the spare works, have a new key cut by a dealer using your VIN, not copied from the worn key.

issues.t: Key won't come out or shifter stuck in Park
issues.sym: The key won't come out of the ignition, or the shifter won't move out of Park.
issues.why: Nissan published a bulletin for the shift lock and key interlock on these vans.
issues.next: Make sure the shifter is fully in Park and the brake pedal is pressed. If it keeps happening, have the dealer repair the interlock using the bulletin.

issues.t: Doors hard to close in freezing weather
issues.sym: After the van sits below freezing, doors won't latch or are hard to close.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin for door latches that stiffen in the cold.
issues.next: Don't slam the doors repeatedly. Ask a dealer about the bulletin repair for the latches.

issues.t: Weak air conditioning in the rear seats
issues.sym: Passengers in the back get little or no cool air, and the rear can be much hotter than the front on hot days.
issues.why: Owners report weak rear airflow, failed rear blower motors and dealers finding no fault. Cooling for the rear relies on airflow from the front system.
issues.next: Have the blower, cabin filter and A/C charge checked. Don't leave children or pets in the back on hot days.

issues.t: Hood flies open while driving
issues.sym: The hood pops up at speed and can smash into the windshield.
issues.why: Owners reported hood latch failures on early vans.
issues.next: Check that the hood is fully latched by pulling up on it after closing. Have the latch and safety catch inspected and lubricated.

issues.t: Engine vibration from driver-side mount
issues.sym: Vibration felt in the cabin at idle or a thump when shifting into gear.
issues.why: Nissan issued updated parts information for the driver-side engine mount on these vans.
issues.next: Have the engine mounts checked. Replace a worn mount before it lets the engine move enough to stress other parts.

issues.t: No start from low 12-volt battery
issues.sym: The van clicks or won't crank, especially after sitting a few days, with no other obvious problem.
issues.why: Nissan issued bulletins on no-starts caused by low battery voltage and on how to test the 12-volt battery. Short trips and accessories on work vans drain it.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested. Use a battery maintainer if the van sits, and replace a weak battery before winter.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge shows the wrong level, so you can run out of gas unexpectedly.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin for an inaccurate fuel gauge with stored engine computer codes.
issues.next: Track mileage between fill-ups until it's fixed, and ask the dealer about the fuel gauge bulletin.
